name: Battle of Mohács

phases.title: The two armies take up their positions
phases.text: The Hungarians stood in two lines on a waterlogged plain, mercenary infantry and artillery in the centre of the first with heavy cavalry on both flanks, and levy infantry and reserve cavalry behind. The Ottomans faced them with Ibrahim Pasha in the centre.

phases.title: The Hungarian cavalry charges the Ottoman front
phases.text: In the early afternoon Archbishop Pál Tomori led a charge that drove back the Ottoman front line and caused disorder among the irregulars. The Ottoman centre gave ground.

phases.title: The Ottoman centre falls back and the reserves follow
phases.text: Ibrahim Pasha's centre fell back in a controlled manoeuvre and formed a crescent that exposed the flanks of the advancing cavalry. King Louis and the reserves moved in support, and the Hungarian centre advanced as well.

phases.title: The Ottoman wings counterattack and the guns open fire
phases.text: The Ottomans struck with cavalry and light infantry from both wings, while Janissaries and artillery fired from prepared positions. The Hungarian army had advanced too far and too fast.

phases.title: The Hungarian army is encircled and its lines collapse
phases.text: Surrounded and under concentrated musket and cannon fire, the Hungarian army collapsed within two hours. Over 14,000 Hungarian troops died by one estimate.

note: The accounts do not give compass directions, so none is drawn. The Hungarians are drawn on the left and the Ottomans on the right. Where the marsh and the Csele stream lay is not stated: they are placed behind the Hungarian line, where the story needs them, and the village of Mohács is not drawn. The Ottoman wings and the Janissaries are placed by judgement, since the accounts say only that the counterattack came from both wings and that the Janissaries and artillery fired from prepared positions. The accounts put the Ottoman strength at perhaps 45,000 fighting troops, or perhaps 50,000, with some historians saying 100,000. One report has Suleiman struck on his cuirass by bullets during the charge; the plan does not show it. King Louis drowned near the Csele stream while trying to flee; his flight is not drawn.
